posts.text:
Six days in June 1967. Each band on this map is territory that changed hands on a single day. By the last one, Israel held roughly three times the land it started the week with.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The trigger came before any shooting. In May 1967 Nasser expelled the UN force from Sinai, massed troops on the border, and on 22-23 May closed the Straits of Tiran to Israeli shipping. Israel had said since 1957 that closing them meant war.

2/ The war was largely decided in its first hours. Operation Focus struck Egyptian airfields on the morning of 5 June and destroyed around 338 Egyptian aircraft, most of them on the ground. Israel lost 19 planes and held the sky for the rest of the week.

3/ The edge was almost boring: turnaround time. Israeli ground crews had drilled rearming and refuelling until one jet could fly up to four sorties a day, against one or two in Arab air forces. Same aircraft, wave after wave.

4/ Jordan was dragged in by a pact signed on 30 May. King Hussein's artillery opened fire on 5 June and within two days he had lost East Jerusalem and the West Bank: the band marked 7th June on the map.

5/ Egypt's front collapsed faster. Nasser ordered Sinai evacuated, and by 8 June Israel stood on the Suez Canal. Sinai alone is about 60,000 km², roughly three times the size of Israel before the war.

6/ The Golan is the strangest part of the map. Syria announced it accepted a ceasefire at 3am on 9 June. Four hours later Moshe Dayan ordered the assault anyway, without government authorisation. The 9th and 10th June bands are that decision.

7/ Six days, and the borders it drew are still the ones being argued over. Over 15,000 Arab dead, fewer than 1,000 Israeli. Roughly 280,000-325,000 Palestinians and 100,000 Syrians fled or were expelled.

Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
